title: Sid Meier's Pirates!
text: Brilliant pirate game, especially on a laptop on a slow day. Nice and simple. Well, I say simple. There are a number of mini-games and mechanics that you simply have to figure out yourself, but it is quite a simple little game. Less than a gig. The cartoonish art style holds up well and doesn't look any worse when you're forced to turn off Shadows to get your frames back. I've had a few hard crashes, and alt+tabbing out causes a runtime error, but the autosave is brilliant so it's not much of a frustration. Though, the base controls require either a numpad or professional level mouse response on an on-screen interface. I found a way to rebind some controls after a couple hours hunting through forumns across the interwebs, but it's not brilliant. So it's not perfect. But I'm having a blast with it and if you're even bothering to read reviews then you will too. I'd advise waiting for a sale, it's pretty bare-bones for any more than $10.

title: Silent Hunter 5®: Battle of the Atlantic
text: Remember everything that you loved about the Silent Hunter series?  Good, hold on to those memories, because this game has got none of that going on. In a sad attempt to make things more "cinematic" they force you into a first person mode through the entire game.  Want to check your map?  Walk to the map room.  Want to check periscope?  Walk over to the periscope and push a bunch of buttons.  Want to make a lightning fast surface raid on an unescorted convoy? Tell helm to surface, manually lower periscope, climb up two ladders through the conning tower, open the hatch, climb out (to find two other guys already up there, somehow), climb back down the outside of the tower, walk over to the deck gun and manually fire it.  Uh oh, an enemy destroyer appeared?  Need to crash dive?  Walk back to the tower, climb up the outside... yeah, you get the picture. You're not the captain.  You're a crewman.  In fact, you are crewman.  You are running that entire submarine yourself in a room full of animatronic mannequins.  It's like being on the wrong end of some u-boat creepypasta, the eternally damned captain on a ship full of ghosts or something, doomed to repeat the same dull sequence of needless actions for eternity. This series peaked at 3, nose dived at 4, and now at 5 has finally come to rest at the bottom.  The graphics have never been better and the gameplay has never been worse.  I could go into the details on the bugs, the incomplete features, the downright wrongness of so many of the games dates & stats, but I don't feel like writing another sixty paragraphs nor should I have to.  Even if it your typical Ubisoft pile of spaghetti code it would still be a thumbs down just for having such flaccid gameplay to begin with.

title: Silent Hunter 5®: Battle of the Atlantic
Silent Hunter 5®: Battle of the Atlantic
text: If you buy this game, be prepared to fight two wars at once; one against the British and the other against the game controls and interface. The latter seems to pose the greatest threat.  Silent Hunter 5 reeks of a game that has been rushed out the door in order to meet a deadline. The game is no more finished than an early beta release, but is being sold as a completed project. That's unfortunate because this game could have been a gem. Missing are some of the basic controls you would expect in a submarine simulator. For example, you have no way of checking your depth under keel. This remarkable oversight would have sent every sub in WWII to the bottom, literally. There is no way to adjust game controls such as mouse tracking speed. This is incredibly frustrating since the tracking speed while in first person is incredibly slow. The AI is unpredictable and often just plain stupid. The safety of your home port is the most dangerous place in the game, as friendly ships will slam right into you with no attempt to avert the disaster. This is especially prevalant while time warping. You have to always save the game before time warping, otherwise you will find you ship destroyed due to the game's failure to pull you out of time warp when there is a danger (as it is supposed to do). Once my time warp was ended with the crew screaming about damage that had been sustained to the ship. That's not unusual. That happens all the time when the game fails stop time warping. However, what was most interesting was the fact that my boat was inexplicably on dry land, well inland. The graphics are, at times, absolutely gorgeous. It's to the point where I think the developers spent way too much time working on the graphics and didn't have enough time left to work on the interface. Fortunately, there is a modding community out there working on the countless bugs. If you choose to buy this game, you will need them. I'm just sad that this game, which is actually fun and interesting, was shoved out the door for the sake of a quick buck. I would only recommend this game to hardcore submarine or WWII enthusiasts who don't mind tweaking and modding the game to get it working halfway decently.

When the game first came out it was among the first to have must-have-internet and that time it was avoided by alot for that. That was years ago and constant internet connections are now very common. Seems to lag when docked with the lighting and the people. This is on a good gaming rig of 2016. I could only imagine how buggy that would have been in the early years. Not sure even if there are tutorials but Im sure there alot of guides and lets play now. Ive sub simmed alot so even managed to fuddle through a manual TDC (torpedo data computer). If you haven't done one of those before you definitely need to have a tutorial, guide or video watch. The critical issue warning is that Steam and Uplay don't connect well. There are some guides and this is a quick one I did. 1) download and setup SH5 2) try playing and if you get a Uplay error thats their internet connection service 3) Goto Ubisoft, set up an account, download Uplay and install 4) Have uplay logged in when you next try to start SH5 Thats what worked for me. On a scale of 1-10 id put things over all at a 6.5 compared to modern options. Still playable, fun and a neat setting. Got it now as part of the Xmas sale and for an onsale game Id rate it 8 out of 10.  Very functional though the few hiccups tend to break my immersion at times.

text: SimplePlanes offers quite a bit for a small package. It teaches the essentials of flight and gives you a very gummy build style with the core pieces to redesign quite a few aircraft and vehicles or come up with your own designs. Gameplay: Mostly a simple vehicle sandbox based around flight physics, it does feel almost like a bit of an actual simulation more then you may be led onto believe. One of the most beautiful aspects of this entire game is all of its user-friendly design, from crafting to flying, and most notably the GUI itself- You can learn it all in about 2 minutes. Campaign: It offers a quick set of GUI and gameplay tutorials along with challanges and also a sandbox mode, as well as a 'quick combat' mode of dog fighting and bombing targets. I would recommend this: To any one who wants to fly some planes/jets/VTOLS quickly, learn the essentials of flight most-accurately, and enjoy having some dog fights against AI or bomb some ground targets---- Or not bomb anything and just build, think and fly!

title: SimplePlanes
text: I wanted to like this game. The concept is great and it has a lot of promise, in that you can custom-build a variety of aircraft and ground vehicles. However, there are two giant show-stoppers that made me refund the game. Awful physics engine - for a game that's about aircraft, the developers could've put more effort into a better physics engine. Controls - The controls are just awful; rudders jolt your plane back and forth, and the mouse movement is inconsistent. Really unfortunate, this game has lots of promise.

title: SimplePlanes
text: This is the type of game that can suck up tons and tons of hours while you sit there picking through parts, adjusting them to size and fitting them to different creations.  And all this is long before you give those creations a test drive.  And this is also considering how many designs you have to go through just to make one that has decent physics and will stay in the air lol!  I love this game!  Unfortunately, I dont have the spare hours in life to play this game as much as Id like.  I still love it though.  Ive designed a few of my own vehicles in the 15hrs Ive played but mostly I like to download a community design and play around with it-again, primarily because of the time constraints in my real life.  Do I recommend this game?  Definitely!  I think the only folk who wouldnt are those with ADHD and expect instant results/gratification from their games.  This game is a designers dream.  And the dream of anyone who ever thought Leggos were the greatest invention ever as a kid.

title: SimplePlanes
text: OK, this is pretty cool.  While it isn't classified as early access, it is still under development. The design tools are far more robust than Kerbal's; I have wanted everything in this game in KSP's vanilla parts for years. However, what's currently in Simple Planes is very basic.  You design a plane or vehicle, take it into a quick combat mission or test drive... and that's it.  It's like a crate of unique LEGO parts with only one building plate, still impressive but you can only do so much. I hope the community adds more maps, and apparently multiplayer support is coming.  Hopefully it isn't too little too late.

title: Sine Mora
text: This is a spoilerfree review of the game played on the easyest difficulty. This was easyly the best shmup I have ever played. The story contains time manipulation so it is rather hard to follow, after you beat the game you get an encyclopedia though that gives informations about the game world. that kind of makes it easyer, the wikipedia article on the game erases any questions that should have remained. Anyway, aside from time being part of the story it is also a game mechanic, as you can slow down time when the hell the bullets put you in is to big. it has a meter though so you cant just slowmo yourself through the game. There is also a limited amount of time you have before dying that gets a few extra seconds every time you kill an enemy and that gets reduced when you are hit, so its also kind of your health. aside from that you really just shoot the stoff coming at you and dodge what you cant shoot, with different subweapons depeding on the  pilot and you pick up powerups on the way. after death you have a limited amount of continues that let you start again from the last checkpoint (though I often had moments of "WHAT? Way back there was the last checkpoint? god damnit") if you get a total gameover you only have to restart a story chapter not the entire thing. That description doesnt do the game justice though. What amazed me is the variety the game offers. You will never really encounter the same enemy for to long, the areas all feel unique and all of it looks gorgeous. the bossfights are numerous and epic, like seriously you get thrown against one epic machine of doom after another. I cant say anything about the difficult difficulties, I do know however, that even the easyest difficulty will sometimes require restarting a chapter because it still is bullethellish after all. The downsides: First and foremost the length. If you dont play this to get all the achievements, if you dont play this failing every 20 seconds because you chose a difficulty that is way to high for you, then you should, like me, get two hours out of this. those may be the best two hours you have ever had with a shmup but it is still questionable if that is worth 10 euros/dollars/billion simbabwe dollars/whatever. so I would reccomend waiting for a sale. btw I checked on the achievement guide, and if you want to get all of those you can count on 50 hours or more worth of gametime. I think id quickly lose the fun in that though. my second problem is a technical issue that maybe I was just to blind to see the fix for in the option: the mouse if I wanted to fly accross the screen my plane was always one sluggish ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥forcing me repeteadly flail my mouse across the desk to dodge the bullets fast enough. yeah thats it, really cant think of anything negative except for that.

title: Sine Mora
text: So I've only played a bit, but it's an OK Shump.  For $2. US it's more than worth it.   Graphics are great.  Gameplay seems so-so.  I could REALLY do without the stupidity of the "hurry up" timer that dogs you the entire time, and the fact that even minor hits cause you to drop your weapon upgrades.  Also if you die/continue you start with no upgrades.  Might as well start the entire thing over at that point (especially on a boss) Audio is non-English (Hungarian perhaps?)  with English subtitles.  Controls are MUCH better with an external controller. The keyboard makes it fairly difficult to get through the levels where analog control to steer through a narrow channel really shines. Graphics are great.  Looks great on a large TV. Forums report numerous bugs.  Devs are long gone. Who knows who gets the $ but won't patch it. Overall: 6/10.  For $2 it was a steal.  Grab it while you can. TLDR: It's not Gunbirds, Gigawing, or even Ikaruga.  (and can't touch Radiant Silvergun or DonPachi) but it's a pretty damn fun Shump with hot graphics and some annoying design.

title: Sine Mora
text: The difficulty of the first playthrough could have you thinking this game is just some sparkly, dumbed-down space shooter for the masses (In fact it's the only one I was ever able to complete).  But holy hell does that change immediately thereafter.  I was not up to that insane challenge. The graphics really are stellar though, with creative and diverse levels.  The control is super tight, the power up mechanics work great and the bosses are epic. The writing is well above par and I really dug how the game was not voiced in English.  Made it feel more "gritty."

title: Sine Mora
text: I never played any other shoot em up, so I don't have any other game to compare. So where do I begin. There are some trial and error, where you need to die to even to know that there was something coming, like train insta' killing you right at the beginning of the level. The campaign is short (around 3h), although it's clear that the main part in games like this is in arcade mode to beat records, it still could be little bit longer. The campaign has interesting story, something that would fit better on some scifi RPG than on shoot em up game. It's strange that the last boss is way too easy, many of the minibosses are much harder. It's good little game to play on short 15-30 min sessions, longer than that just makes the game harder, as too many instakills makes you angry and then loose you're focus.
